arxiv-2012-08832.title: Heavy Ions Experimental Overview
arxiv-2012-08832.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by *. This article gives an overview of recent highlights from experimental measurements of heavy-ion collisions at ultra-relativistic energies: Measurements of electroweak probes constrain both the initial collision geometry and the nuclear parton distribution functions. Results from soft particle production show that the abundance of light-flavour hadrons from pions up to hypertriton and 4 He can be described by a universal temperature and that these participate in the collective motion of the system.

arxiv-2311-16570.title: Epistemic Limits of Empirical Finance: Causal Reductionism and Self-Reference
arxiv-2311-16570.creator: Daniel Polakow, Tim Gebbie, Emlyn Flint
arxiv-2311-16570.description: Abstract The clarion call for causal reduction in the study of capital markets is intensifying. However, in self-referencing and open systems such as capital markets, the idea of unidirectional causation (if applicable) may be limiting at best, and unstable or fallacious at worst.

arxiv-2401-03345.title: Volatility models in practice: Rough, Path-dependent or Markovian?
arxiv-2401-03345.creator: Eduardo Abi Jaber, Shaun (Xiaoyuan) Li
arxiv-2401-03345.description: Abstract We present an empirical study examining several claims related to option prices in rough volatility literature using SPX options data. Our results show that rough volatility models with the parameter H ∈ ( 0 , 1 / 2 ) H\in(0,1/2) are inconsistent with the global shape of SPX smiles.

arxiv-2404-06185.title: Wess-Zumino-Witten Terms of S ​ p Sp QCD by Bordism Theory
arxiv-2404-06185.creator: Shota Saito
arxiv-2404-06185.description: Abstract We investigate the four-dimensional Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) terms within the framework of S ​ p Sp quantum chromodynamics (QCD) using invertible field theory through bordism theory. We present a novel approach aimed at circumventing both perturbative and non-perturbative gauge anomalies on spacetime manifolds endowed with spin structures.

arxiv-2404-19567.title: Causal Perception Inspired Representation Learning for Trustworthy Image Quality Assessment
arxiv-2404-19567.creator: Lei Wang, Desen Yuan
arxiv-2404-19567.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Lei Wang, Desen Yuan. Despite great success in modeling visual perception, deep neural network based image quality assessment (IQA) still remains unreliable in real-world applications due to its vulnerability to adversarial perturbations and the inexplicit black-box structure. In this paper, we propose to build a trustworthy IQA model via Causal Perception inspired Representation Learning (CPRL), and a score reflection attack method for IQA model. More specifically, we assume that each image is composed of Causal Perception Representation (CPR) and non-causal perception representation (N-CPR).

arxiv-2409-06108.title: Efficiently catching entangled microwave photons from a quantum transducer with shaped optical pumps
arxiv-2409-06108.creator: Changchun Zhong
arxiv-2409-06108.description: Abstract Quantum transducer, when working as a microwave and optical entanglement generator, provides a practical way of coherently connecting optical communication channels and microwave quantum processors. The recent experiments on quantum transducer verifying entanglement between microwave and optical photons show the promise of approaching that goal.

arxiv-2412-17739.title: Fourier Position Embedding: Enhancing Attention’s Periodic Extension for Length Generalization
arxiv-2412-17739.creator: Ermo Hua, Che Jiang, Xingtai Lv, Kaiyan Zhang, Ning Ding, Youbang Sun, Biqing Qi, Yuchen Fan, Xuekai Zhu, Bowen Zhou
arxiv-2412-17739.description: Abstract Extending the context length of Language Models (LMs) by improving Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) has become a trend. While existing works mainly address RoPE’s limitations within attention mechanism, this paper provides an analysis across nearly all parts of LMs, uncovering their adverse effects on length generalization for RoPE-based attention.

arxiv-2502-12972.title: Skip That Beat: Augmenting Meter Tracking Models for Underrepresented Time Signatures
arxiv-2502-12972.description: Abstract Beat and downbeat tracking models are predominantly developed using datasets with music in 4/4 meter, which decreases their generalization to repertories in other time signatures, such as Brazilian samba which is in 2/4. In this work, we propose a simple augmentation technique to increase the representation of time signatures beyond 4/4, namely 2/4 and 3/4.

arxiv-2508-17241.title: Model Theory of General von Neumann Algebras I: Generalized Ocneanu Ultraproducts
arxiv-2508-17241.creator: Jananan Arulseelan
arxiv-2508-17241.description: Abstract . This paper collates, presents, and expands upon technology and results obtained as part of the author’s PhD thesis. We generalize work done in the σ \sigma -finite setting by the author, Goldbring, Hart, and Sinclair by producing a language and axiomatization of full left Hilbert algebras.

arxiv-2511-09815.title: Traversable wormhole with double trace deformations via gravitational shear and sound channels
arxiv-2511-09815.creator: Fitria Khairunnisa, Hadyan Luthfan Prihadi, M. Zhahir Djogama, Donny Dwiputra, Freddy Permana Zen
arxiv-2511-09815.description: Abstract We investigate how non-local gravitational couplings from double-trace deformation between two asymptotic boundaries of an AdS 5 black brane can lead to the violation of the Averaged Null Energy Condition (ANEC). The first-order gravitational perturbations backreact with the background metric at second-order, creating a wormhole opening.

arxiv-2602-11923.title: The Radius Cliff is a Waterfall: Explaining Sub-Neptune Exoplanets with Steam Worlds
arxiv-2602-11923.creator: Aritra Chakrabarty, Gijs D. Mulders, Artyom Aguichine, Natalie Batalha
arxiv-2602-11923.description: Abstract The demographics of Kepler planets provide a key testbed for models of planet formation and evolution, particularly for explaining the radius valley separating super-Earths and sub-Neptunes. A primordial interpretation based on differences in bulk densities—where rocky and water-rich planets form via migration pathways—offers an alternative to atmospheric loss scenarios.

pmc-10504711.title: Factors influencing the quality of acupuncture clinical trials: a qualitative interview of stakeholders
pmc-10504711.creator: Ying He, Nian Li, Qin Wang, Ying Wang, Zelei Dai, Miaomiao Wu, Haiqi Song, Qian Wen, Ning Li, Yonggang Zhang
pmc-10504711.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the influencing factors on the quality of acupuncture clinical trials from the stakeholders, and to provide references for improving the quality of acupuncture clinical trials.MethodsA qualitative study based on semi-structured interviews was performed. Experts, acupuncturists, editors, and patients were interviewed. The interview results were thematically analyzed from transcribed audio recordings.

pmc-10533502.title: Application of Pt@ZIF-8 nanocomposite-based electrochemical biosensor for sensitive diagnosis of tau protein in Alzheimer’s disease patients
pmc-10533502.creator: Forough Chakari-Khiavi, Arezoo Mirzaie, Balal Khalilzadeh, Hadi Yousefi, Rozita Abolhasan, Amin Kamrani, Ramin Pourakbari, Koorosh Shahpasand, Mehdi Yousefi, Mohammad-Reza Rashidi
pmc-10533502.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive brain disorder characterized by the ongoing decline of brain functions. Studies have revealed the detrimental effects of hyperphosphorylated tau (p-tau) protein fibrils in AD pathogenesis, highlighting the importance of this factor in the early-stage detection of AD conditions.

pmc-10659028.title: Machine Learning-Based Screening for Potential Singlet Fission Chromophores: The Challenge of Imbalanced Data Sets
pmc-10659028.creator: Lyuben Borislavov, Miroslava Nedyalkova, Alia Tadjer, Onder Aydemir, Julia Romanova
pmc-10659028.description: Excitation with one photon of a singlet fission (SF) material generates two triplet excitons, thus doubling the solar cell efficiency. Therefore, the SF molecules are regarded as new generation organic photovoltaics, but it is hard to identify them. Recently, it was demonstrated that molecules of low-to-intermediate diradical character (DRC) are potential SF chromophores.

pmc-11360523.title: A Buffered Local Anesthetic Without Epinephrine: Development, Characterization, and In Vivo Efficacy and Toxicity Analysis
pmc-11360523.creator: Daniel Uzbelger Feldman, Billy B Laun, Chirag Patel, Sonal V Pande, Sai H S Boddu, Neal M Davies
pmc-11360523.description: Lidocaine hydrochloride (HCl) 2% with 1:100,000 epinephrine (LW/E) is widely used to prevent pain during dental procedures and has been associated with injection sting, jittering effects, slow onset, and a bitter aftertaste. Since LW/E’s introduction in 1948, no significant modifications have been proposed.

pmc-11429811.title: Locked in Structure: Sestrin and GATOR—A Billion-Year Marriage
pmc-11429811.creator: Alexander Haidurov, Andrei V Budanov, Christian Neri
pmc-11429811.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Sestrins are a conserved family of stress-responsive proteins that play a crucial role in cellular metabolism, stress response, and ageing. Vertebrates have three Sestrin genes (SESN1, SESN2, and SESN3), while invertebrates encode only one. Initially identified as antioxidant proteins that regulate cell viability, Sestrins are now recognised as crucial inhibitors of the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 kinase (mTORC1), a central regulator of anabolism, cell growth, and autophagy.

pmc-11472796.title: A dose‐adjusted, open‐label, pilot study of the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of STC3141 in critically ill patients with sepsis
pmc-11472796.creator: Rinaldo Bellomo, John Patava, Ruth Van Lancker, Nathalie Layios, Marijke Peetermans, Mark Plummer, Rachid Attou, Robert McNamara, Andrew Udy, Bradley Wibrow, Adam Deane, Edward Litton, Marcel Tanudji, Fuhong Su, Zhang Zhong, Linda Shi, Li Ning
pmc-11472796.description: Increased circulating histones correlate with sepsis severity and are a potential therapeutic target. Pre‐clinical studies showed benefit with a histone‐neutralizing polyanion molecule (STC3141). We aimed to investigate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of STC3141 in critically ill patients with sepsis. We studied 26 patients with sepsis divided into four cohorts of one, five, ten, and ten subjects, respectively.

pmc-11508127.title: Synergistic Proliferation Effects of Xanthohumol and Niflumic Acid on Merkel and Glioblastoma Cancer Cells: Role of Cell Membrane Interactions
pmc-11508127.creator: Monika Stompor-Gorący, Aleksandra Włoch, Priti Sengupta, Anna Nasulewicz-Goldeman, Joanna Wietrzyk, Jan Korabecny
pmc-11508127.description: The objective of our research was to determine the effects of xanthohumol (XN), a flavonoid isolated from hops (Humulus lupulus), and the anti-inflammatory drug niflumic acid (NA), separately and in combination with each other, on the proliferation of human cancer cells.

pmc-11716575.title: Brain Functional Flexibility and its Relationship to the Preclinical Stage of Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-11716575.creator: Mohammadali Javanray, Frederic St‐Onge, Pierre Bellec, Bratislav Misic, Jean‐Paul Soucy, Sylvia Villeneuve, PEREVNT‐AD Research Group
pmc-11716575.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundCharacterizing pathological and functional features of the preclinical stage of Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is essential as Amyloid beta (Aβ) and tau, the pathological hallmarks of AD, start to accumulate years prior to the onset of clinical symptoms.

pmc-12549783.title: Wireless trigger distribution with nanosecond jitter based on ultra-wideband transceiver modules
pmc-12549783.creator: Julius Korsimaa, Martin Weber, Edward Hæggström, Ari Salmi
pmc-12549783.description: Wireless sensor networks require time synchronization to operate in a coordinated manner. Synchronizing the clock of each sensor node by using a network protocol can be sufficient for millisecond accuracy, whereas precision in the range of nanoseconds can be achieved by using Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receivers.

pmc-13286100.title: Iatrogenic Gastroesophageal Junction Perforation During Emergency Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography in a 91-Year-Old Woman with Choledocholithiasis and Cholangitis
pmc-13286100.creator: Songming Ding, Yangjun Gu, Yang Liu, Shusen Zheng, Qiyong Li
pmc-13286100.description: perforation is a life-threatening complication. 2​ We report a case of iatrogenic GEJ perforation occurring during emergency ERCP in a 91-year-old woman, which was successfully managed with immediate endoscopic clipping. The patient presented with a 2-week history of abdominal pain and a 1-day history of fever. Physical examination revealed a temperature of 39.1°C and epigastric tenderness.

pmc-13619760.title: Post Hoc Subgroup and Body Region Analyses of VASI Outcomes Among Patients with Vitiligo in a Phase 2 Povorcitinib Trial
pmc-13619760.creator: Thierry Passeron, Amit G. Pandya, Khaled Ezzedine, Nanja van Geel, Lois Erskine, Leandro L. Santos, Zhenyi Xue, Andrew Blauvelt
pmc-13619760.description: IntroductionA phase 2 trial (NCT04818346) of the oral Janus kinase 1 inhibitor povorcitinib demonstrated substantial total body and facial repigmentation over 52 weeks in adults with extensive nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV). Here, post hoc analyses evaluated povorcitinib efficacy in patients based on demographic and clinical characteristic subgroups, as well as affected body regions.

pmc-13630615.title: A prediction model based on the prognostic nutritional index for grade 2 or higher radiation-induced oral mucositis in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma
pmc-13630615.creator: Deyue Jiang, Ruohan Wang, Jin Lu, Huanhuan Yu, Haoxuan Zhang
